summary.oneLiner: Adani Enterprises is rapidly scaling an integrated infrastructure and green energy ecosystem, with incubating businesses now contributing nearly half of EBITDA, driven by domestic manufacturing breakthroughs in solar, wind, and green hydrogen, while leveraging its mining and logistics moat to fund capital-intensive transitions. The company is on track to become a vertically integrated clean energy powerhouse with global export potential.
summary.business: Adani Enterprises Limited incubates and nurtures emerging infrastructure businesses that contribute to nation-building and economic growth, having previously scaled and separately listed industry-leading entities including Adani Ports & SEZ, Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy and Adani Total Gas. Its current portfolio spans Integrated Resources Management (mineral procurement & logistics), the New Energy Ecosystem (green hydrogen and derivatives, solar cells/modules, wind turbine generators and electrolysers via wholly-owned subsidiary Adani New Industries Limited), Copper smelting and refining, Airport and Road construction/operation/maintenance, Commercial Mining, Mining Services (Mine Development & Operations), and Defence & Aerospace manufacturing. The Company and its subsidiaries primarily serve B2B customers across Integrated Resources Management, Mining Services, New Energy Ecosystem, Defence & Aerospace, Data Centers and Copper, while operating a B2C model for its Airports and Road businesses; the next phase of investment is focused on high-growth sectors including the new energy ecosystem, airport management, data centers, roads, and primary industries like copper and PVC.

currentContext.strengths: Group 'incubator' model: AEL has a demonstrated track record of incubating early-stage infrastructure businesses and scaling them into industry-leading, separately-listed entities (Adani Ports & SEZ, Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy, Adani Total Gas), giving it a repeatable playbook for entering new high-growth sectors such as the new energy ecosystem, airports, data centers, roads, copper and PVC|Backward-integrated New Energy value chain: ANIL is building in-house electrolyser manufacturing at Mundra (including its own Electrolyser Testing Laboratory), which the Company states strengthens quality control, optimises costs, and supports higher-performance electrolysers versus sourcing components externally|Adani Solar has a proven execution track record, strong customer relationships and process-driven manufacturing, positioning it as a trusted supplier to both domestic and export markets; it was an early adopter of TOPCon cell technology in India and operates high-efficiency automated mono PERC (up to 23.2%) and TOPCon (average 25.3%) cell lines|Cross-group infrastructure integration: the Company describes an ability to import fuel through group-owned ports, feed group mining output into power generation, move power over an extensive group-owned transmission grid, and locate data-centre cable-landing stations within group-owned ports with land secured via the group's real-estate arm|Policy-linked cost/demand support: ANIL was awarded SECI Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) support for domestic electrolyser manufacturing capacity, and Adani Solar benefits from India's Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) ecosystem plus captive demand from within the Adani Group|Diversified, predominantly B2B customer base spanning Integrated Resources Management, Mining Services, New Energy, Defence & Aerospace, Data Centers and Copper, complemented by B2C exposure through Airports and Roads

currentContext.expansion: AEL's growth capex is concentrated in its New Energy Ecosystem (ANIL), Data Centers (AdaniConneX/ACX), Water (AWL) and 'incubating' core infra businesses (Airports/AAHL, Roads/ARTL, Copper/KCL, PVC/MPL, and coal mining). In New Energy: ANIL commissioned India's first off-grid 5 MW Green Hydrogen Pilot Plant in Kutch, Gujarat in June 2025, powered by solar with battery storage, described as a proof of concept for ANIL's upcoming New Energy Hub at Mundra, Gujarat; ANIL targets a Green Hydrogen production capacity of 1 MMTPA (equivalent to 5.6 MMTPA of Green Ammonia) by 2030, in line with the National Green Hydrogen Mission. ANIL is also building an integrated electrolyser manufacturing ecosystem at Mundra designed for 5 GW of electrolysers annually, and has been awarded a SECI PLI incentive for 300 MW of annual electrolyser manufacturing capacity (Tranche I & II). In solar manufacturing, Adani Solar currently operates 4 GW of cell capacity, 4 GW of module capacity and 2 GW of ingot-wafer capacity; an additional 6 GW of TOPCon cell and 6 GW of module capacity is under construction and planned for commissioning in FY 2026-27, taking cumulative capacity to 10 GW of cells and 10 GW of modules as part of a fully automated solar manufacturing ecosystem at Mundra. In wind, ANIL offers four WTG models (2.25 GW manufacturing capacity), secured external orders for 300 MW under its 3.3 MW platform, and supplied 231 WTG sets (including 51 of the 3.3 MW model) during the year, with plans to expand into new domestic and international regions. In Data Centers, AdaniConneX (a 50:50 JV between Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX) has a cumulative order book of 560+ MW, of which 55+ MW is operational across Chennai, Noida, Hyderabad and Pune; it completed and handed over 19.2 MW of capacity to hyperscale customers during the year, with facilities under development at four locations progressing on schedule, and it announced a partnership with Google to develop India's largest AI Data Center campus in Visakhapatnam. ACX targets 2 GW of renewable-powered, tied-up Data Center capacity by 2030 and is expanding hyperscale campuses in Pune, Noida and Hyderabad. The Water business, run through wholly-owned subsidiary Adani Water Limited (AWL), is positioned in wastewater treatment, irrigation infrastructure, river interlinking, large-scale water supply/distribution and desalination projects, though the provided text does not disclose specific AWL projects, capacities or timelines. Among core infra businesses driving the rise in net external debt, the Company cited: commencement of operations at the greenfield Navi Mumbai International Airport; inauguration of the integrated new terminal building at Guwahati airport, alongside a proposed expansion of Guwahati's LGBIA to 18 MPPA passenger handling and 0.15 MTPA cargo handling capacity (EIA conducted, dated 04-Sep-2025); an amendment to the environmental clearance for non-operational (landside) area development at Mumbai's CSMIA; completion of the greenfield Ganga Expressway project and three HAM road assets; construction of a 500 KTPA Copper plant (KCL) with production now ramping up; and construction of a 1 MMTPA PVC plant (MPL). Management stated that EBITDA from these under-construction/ramping assets is expected to be unlocked from the next fiscal year (FY27). Separately, in natural resources, the Company/its group entities obtained environmental clearance (15-04-2025) for the Gondbahera Ujheni Underground Coal mine (4.12/6.18 MTPA normative/peak capacity, Madhya Pradesh) and clearance was recommended (EAC meeting, Sept 2025) for the adjacent Gondbahera Ujheni East Coal Mine.

risks.risk: Chronic physical climate risk — heat stress
risks.note: Rising temperatures reduce equipment efficiency, accelerate infrastructure degradation, and increase maintenance needs; higher cooling demand raises energy consumption and operating costs; prolonged heat exposure lowers worker productivity and raises heat-related illness/safety risk.

risks.risk: Acute physical climate risk — excess rainfall and floods
risks.note: Heavy rainfall/flooding disrupts power and communication services, slows production, delays movement of raw materials and finished goods via blocked/flooded roads, and water stagnation/contamination raises health risks for workers.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Adani Enterprises Limited incubates and nurtures emerging infrastructure businesses that contribute to nation-building and economic growth, having previously scaled and separately listed industry-leading entities including Adani Ports & SEZ, Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy and Adani Total Gas. Its current portfolio spans Integrated Resources Management (mineral procurement & logistics), the New Energy Ecosystem (green hydrogen and derivatives, solar cells/modules, wind turbine generators and electrolysers via wholly-owned subsidiary Adani New Industries Limited), Copper smelting and refining, Airport and Road construction/operation/maintenance, Commercial Mining, Mining Services (Mine Development & Operations), and Defence & Aerospace manufacturing. The Company and its subsidiaries primarily serve B2B customers across Integrated Resources Management, Mining Services, New Energy Ecosystem, Defence & Aerospace, Data Centers and Copper, while operating a B2C model for its Airports and Road businesses; the next phase of investment is focused on high-growth sectors including the new energy ecosystem, airport management, data centers, roads, and primary industries like copper and PVC.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Chairman's letter frames AI/data-centre growth as structurally driving demand for energy, transmission and physical infrastructure ('Before AI can think, energy must flow; before data can move, infrastructure must stand'), underpinning the Group's capital allocation toward energy + data-centre-adjacent infrastructure.
- Airports segment (fragment only, section start not captured in routed text): 'With diversified revenue streams, economies of scale, and substantial organic growth potential, the Airports segment remains a pivotal contributor to the Company's long-term growth trajectory' over the next 2-3 years.
- Roads industry: Union Budget 2026-27 allocated Rs. 3.09 lakh crore to the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (+8% YoY); NHAI constructed 5,313 km of national highways in FY26; highway project execution is expected to accelerate further, supported by Gati Shakti, Bharatmala Pariyojana, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, and revisions to the Model Concession Agreement for HAM projects.
- Roads (ARTL) outlook: with completion of the largest greenfield project (Ganga Expressway), ARTL 'is poised to significantly increase its profitability'; with commencement of the majority of projects, revenue/EBITDA are expected to 'remain stable during the concession period'.
- IRM/coal industry: domestic coal production is estimated to reach 1,210-1,220 MT by FY 2029-30 (from 1,048 MT in FY25); demand from the power and industrial sectors 'continues to outpace supply', sustaining coking/non-coking coal import reliance despite government measures (Single Window Clearance, MMDR Act amendments allowing captive mines to sell up to 50% of output, 100% FDI under automatic route) aimed at boosting domestic production.
- Copper industry: India copper demand grew 9.3% YoY to 1,878 KT in FY 2024-25 (24.1% CAGR over FY20-25), driven by renewables (India's 500 GW renewable-capacity target by 2030), metro-rail/railway electrification, and urbanisation/housing/EV-infrastructure growth — cited as sustaining domestic copper demand.
- Petrochemicals/PVC industry: India's PVC demand-supply gap is estimated at ~2.5 MTPA (demand ~4.3 MTPA vs domestic supply of 1.8 MTPA); India is projected to become one of the largest PVC producers by 2027; demand is expected to be supported by Smart Cities, Housing for All, AMRUT, Jal Jeevan Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission infrastructure programmes.
- Mining Services (MDO) outlook: 'As India's largest MDO, the Company aims to increase volume by 20% in next year', with a stated 'clear long runway available for growth' from its expanded service-contract portfolio; growth is expected to be driven by full-scale digitalisation of operations.
- IRM outlook: business focussed on 'enhancing its capabilities and reach by building a multi-commodity portfolio' and actively seeking partnerships with miners to ensure 'timely and cost-effective resource delivery', aiming for 'long-term sustainable growth'.
- Adani Energy Solutions Limited (Group entity referenced in Chairman's letter): transmission order book rose from Rs. 59,936 crore to Rs. 71,779 crore in FY26; secured major projects including the Khavda-South Olpad HVDC line, and commissioned Mumbai's first VSC-based HVDC project.
- ARTL (Roads) portfolio increased to 20 projects (11 HAM, 5 BOT, 3 TOT, 1 ropeway) after adding six new projects during the year, including the Kedarnath-Son Prayag ropeway project; 13 projects are now operational following commencement of the Ganga Expressway.
- Mining Services portfolio expanded to 18 service contracts with peak capacity of 145.4 MMT per annum; the GP-II mine MDO contract (peak capacity 23.6 MMT per annum) was made operational during the year, taking the operational-contract count to seven.
- A binding MoU was signed with Google for a gigawatt-scale data centre in Visakhapatnam, cited as reflecting global technology-leader confidence in the Group's infrastructure platform.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: AEL's growth capex is concentrated in its New Energy Ecosystem (ANIL), Data Centers (AdaniConneX/ACX), Water (AWL) and 'incubating' core infra businesses (Airports/AAHL, Roads/ARTL, Copper/KCL, PVC/MPL, and coal mining). In New Energy: ANIL commissioned India's first off-grid 5 MW Green Hydrogen Pilot Plant in Kutch, Gujarat in June 2025, powered by solar with battery storage, described as a proof of concept for ANIL's upcoming New Energy Hub at Mundra, Gujarat; ANIL targets a Green Hydrogen production capacity of 1 MMTPA (equivalent to 5.6 MMTPA of Green Ammonia) by 2030, in line with the National Green Hydrogen Mission. ANIL is also building an integrated electrolyser manufacturing ecosystem at Mundra designed for 5 GW of electrolysers annually, and has been awarded a SECI PLI incentive for 300 MW of annual electrolyser manufacturing capacity (Tranche I & II). In solar manufacturing, Adani Solar currently operates 4 GW of cell capacity, 4 GW of module capacity and 2 GW of ingot-wafer capacity; an additional 6 GW of TOPCon cell and 6 GW of module capacity is under construction and planned for commissioning in FY 2026-27, taking cumulative capacity to 10 GW of cells and 10 GW of modules as part of a fully automated solar manufacturing ecosystem at Mundra. In wind, ANIL offers four WTG models (2.25 GW manufacturing capacity), secured external orders for 300 MW under its 3.3 MW platform, and supplied 231 WTG sets (including 51 of the 3.3 MW model) during the year, with plans to expand into new domestic and international regions. In Data Centers, AdaniConneX (a 50:50 JV between Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX) has a cumulative order book of 560+ MW, of which 55+ MW is operational across Chennai, Noida, Hyderabad and Pune; it completed and handed over 19.2 MW of capacity to hyperscale customers during the year, with facilities under development at four locations progressing on schedule, and it announced a partnership with Google to develop India's largest AI Data Center campus in Visakhapatnam. ACX targets 2 GW of renewable-powered, tied-up Data Center capacity by 2030 and is expanding hyperscale campuses in Pune, Noida and Hyderabad. The Water business, run through wholly-owned subsidiary Adani Water Limited (AWL), is positioned in wastewater treatment, irrigation infrastructure, river interlinking, large-scale water supply/distribution and desalination projects, though the provided text does not disclose specific AWL projects, capacities or timelines. Among core infra businesses driving the rise in net external debt, the Company cited: commencement of operations at the greenfield Navi Mumbai International Airport; inauguration of the integrated new terminal building at Guwahati airport, alongside a proposed expansion of Guwahati's LGBIA to 18 MPPA passenger handling and 0.15 MTPA cargo handling capacity (EIA conducted, dated 04-Sep-2025); an amendment to the environmental clearance for non-operational (landside) area development at Mumbai's CSMIA; completion of the greenfield Ganga Expressway project and three HAM road assets; construction of a 500 KTPA Copper plant (KCL) with production now ramping up; and construction of a 1 MMTPA PVC plant (MPL). Management stated that EBITDA from these under-construction/ramping assets is expected to be unlocked from the next fiscal year (FY27). Separately, in natural resources, the Company/its group entities obtained environmental clearance (15-04-2025) for the Gondbahera Ujheni Underground Coal mine (4.12/6.18 MTPA normative/peak capacity, Madhya Pradesh) and clearance was recommended (EAC meeting, Sept 2025) for the adjacent Gondbahera Ujheni East Coal Mine.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Group 'incubator' model: AEL has a demonstrated track record of incubating early-stage infrastructure businesses and scaling them into industry-leading, separately-listed entities (Adani Ports & SEZ, Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy, Adani Total Gas), giving it a repeatable playbook for entering new high-growth sectors such as the new energy ecosystem, airports, data centers, roads, copper and PVC
- Backward-integrated New Energy value chain: ANIL is building in-house electrolyser manufacturing at Mundra (including its own Electrolyser Testing Laboratory), which the Company states strengthens quality control, optimises costs, and supports higher-performance electrolysers versus sourcing components externally
- Adani Solar has a proven execution track record, strong customer relationships and process-driven manufacturing, positioning it as a trusted supplier to both domestic and export markets; it was an early adopter of TOPCon cell technology in India and operates high-efficiency automated mono PERC (up to 23.2%) and TOPCon (average 25.3%) cell lines
- Cross-group infrastructure integration: the Company describes an ability to import fuel through group-owned ports, feed group mining output into power generation, move power over an extensive group-owned transmission grid, and locate data-centre cable-landing stations within group-owned ports with land secured via the group's real-estate arm
- Policy-linked cost/demand support: ANIL was awarded SECI Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) support for domestic electrolyser manufacturing capacity, and Adani Solar benefits from India's Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) ecosystem plus captive demand from within the Adani Group
- Diversified, predominantly B2B customer base spanning Integrated Resources Management, Mining Services, New Energy, Defence & Aerospace, Data Centers and Copper, complemented by B2C exposure through Airports and Roads

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory delays in coal-to-PVC or green hydrogen approvals; Global trade barriers on solar exports (e.g., US tariffs); Execution risk in Navi Mumbai Airport or copper smelter timelines; Volatility in coal prices impacting IRM realization; Competition in domestic solar/wind manufacturing; Currency risk on export revenues

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 33% solar margins are not just from cost savings but from vertical integration and export pricing power; MDO's near-zero inventory implies contractually locked-in demand, making volumes highly predictable; Green hydrogen is being built as a portfolio of cash-positive modules, not a subsidized bet; Navi Mumbai Airport’s schedule is critical for Mumbai’s airport congestion relief — a systemic national infrastructure win
